questions.q: How is a lending pool's utilization calculated?
options: Total supplied divided by total borrowed
The protocol team sets it manually each day
Total borrowed divided by total supplied
Total number of unique depositors in the pool
questions.explain: Utilization = total borrowed / total supplied — the fraction of supplied assets currently lent out.

questions.q: In a kinked interest rate model, what happens to the borrow rate's slope once utilization passes the kink (e.g. 80%)?
options: The rate stops changing entirely above the kink
The slope becomes identical to the slope below the kink
The slope gets much steeper, so the rate rises sharply as utilization climbs further
questions.explain: Above the kink, the curve switches to a much steeper slope — the lesson's example shows the rate climbing from 4% to 75% as utilization goes from 80% to 100%.

questions.q: Why does the interest rate curve deliberately spike hard above the kink, instead of rising gently all the way to 100% utilization?
options: Because a pool that reaches 100% utilization can't process withdrawals, so a steep rate increase is needed to quickly discourage borrowing and attract new supply
To maximize protocol revenue regardless of pool health
Because regulations require a minimum interest rate above 80% utilization
There is no functional reason; it's an arbitrary design choice
questions.explain: A fully utilized pool has no spare liquidity for withdrawals — the steep slope is a deliberate overcorrection meant to pull utilization back down before that happens.

questions.q: At 80% utilization with a 4% borrow rate and a 10% reserve factor, approximately what supply rate do suppliers earn?
questions.explain: Supply rate = borrow rate * utilization * (1 - reserve factor) = 4% * 0.80 * 0.90 = 2.88%.

questions.q: Why is the supply rate always lower than the borrow rate in the same pool?
options: Because supply rates and borrow rates are actually always identical
Because suppliers are charged an extra fee on top of the borrow rate
Because suppliers only earn a share of interest scaled by utilization, and the protocol also takes a reserve factor cut
Because only borrowers are allowed to earn any interest at all
questions.explain: Only the utilized portion of the pool generates interest, and the reserve factor is held back before interest reaches suppliers, so the supply rate is always below the borrow rate.
